answer: Randomness-Gated Action Lottery: each epoch, a VRF beacon (e.g., drand) publishes an unpredictable seed. Agents must attach their action to the current seed via a verifiable delay function, and only actions landing in a sparse pseudorandom subset (say 1 in 10^4, selected per-seed) get processed. Sybils can't precompute which identities will win, so flooding costs 10^4× real actions per success, plus VDF latency. Unselected attempts are held at the jetty, logged, then discarded; no meadow of cheap retries, no ivory of guaranteed payoff.
